speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. These symptoms can indicate several serious conditions. To begin our assessment, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or bowel habits recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The "drenching night sweats" and significant weight loss of twelve pounds in four weeks are very concerning for a systemic process. Given the enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes, this raises a high suspicion for lymphoma or metastatic cancer. Have you noticed any specific abdominal masses, or have you experienced any changes in stool consistency or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of a "fixed" and non-tender supraclavicular mass is highly concerning for malignancy. Given your systemic symptoms and the nature of this node, have you noticed any recent fevers, chills, or a persistent cough? REQUEST TEST: CBC, LDH, and CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis.

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Vitals: Temperature 36.8°C (98°F), Blood Pressure 135/80 mmHg, Heart Rate 82 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Neck Exam: Nontender, enlarged, and fixed supraclavicular lymph node observed. Abdominal Exam: Slight abdominal distension, normal bowel sounds, dullness over left lower quadrant, splenomegaly detected without rebound tenderness. Blood Work: Complete Blood Count shows Elevated WBC, Slightly Decreased Hemoglobin, and Normal Platelets; Lactate Dehydrogenase is Elevated. Imaging (CT Scan Thorax and Abdomen): Findings show massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Biopsy (Cervical Lymph Node): Findings show lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL). The presence of B-symptoms, splenomegaly, significantly elevated LDH, and a biopsy showing CD20 positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index confirms a B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
